slides.title: Prompt Quality Matters
content: A weak prompt gets a weak answer.
A great prompt gets a great answer.
slides.narration:
Have you ever received a poor answer from an AI?
That's because of a weak prompt.
A weak prompt gives a weak answer.
A great prompt gives a great answer.
slides.image_prompt: Split screen: frustrated person with weak AI output vs. happy person with excellent AI output.

slides.title: The 3 Cs of Prompting
content: Clarity
Context
Constraints
slides.narration:
The best prompts include three key ingredients.
These are Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
Let's explore each one.

slides.title: 1. Clarity: Be Specific!
content: AI doesn't know what you're thinking.
Vague prompts lead to generic answers.
slides.narration:
Let's start with Clarity.
Clarity means being specific.
The AI cannot read your mind.
Vague prompts give generic, unhelpful answers.
slides.image_prompt: Magnifying glass focusing on a word 'Specific', with AI robot looking confused.

slides.title: Clarity: Example
content: Weak Prompt: "Write about electric cars."
Good Prompt: "Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
slides.narration:
Let's see an example of a weak prompt.
Type 'Write about electric cars.'
Now, try this clear prompt.
It asks to 'Write a short blog post'.
Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car.
This is for someone living in a city.
See the difference?
slides.image_prompt: Split screen: AI output for 'Write about electric cars' (generic) vs. AI output for the specific prompt (focused).

slides.title: 2. Context: Give Background!
content: Context tells AI why you're asking.
It helps AI adopt the right perspective.
slides.narration:
Next, let's add Context.
Context provides background information.
It tells the AI why you are asking.
This helps the AI adopt the correct perspective.
slides.image_prompt: AI robot wearing different hats (e.g., chef hat, doctor hat, writer hat) to show perspective.

slides.title: Context: Example
content: Good Prompt: "Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
Better Prompt: "Write a short blog post for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."
slides.narration:
Consider our previous good prompt.
Now let's make it better with context.
Add 'for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living.'
The AI now understands the audience.
slides.image_prompt: Split screen: AI output for 'Good Prompt' vs. 'Better Prompt' with more targeted tone.

slides.title: 3. Constraints: Set Rules!
content: Constraints are boundaries for the output.
Tell AI the length, format, and style.
slides.narration:
Finally, we have Constraints.
Constraints set boundaries for the AI's output.
Tell the AI the length, format, and style you need.
This shapes the final answer.
slides.image_prompt: AI robot building blocks within a defined box, symbolizing boundaries.

slides.title: Constraints: Example
content: Better Prompt: "Write a short blog post for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city."

Excellent Prompt: "Write a short blog post, under 400 words, for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city. Use a friendly and enthusiastic tone and end with a question to encourage comments."
slides.narration:
Let's take our better prompt.
Now, add some constraints.
Specify 'under 400 words'.
Also, 'use a friendly and enthusiastic tone'.
And 'end with a question'.
This gives a highly refined output.
slides.image_prompt: Split screen: AI output for 'Better Prompt' vs. 'Excellent Prompt' showing word count, tone, and concluding question.

slides.title: Bonus Tip: Persona
content: Tell the AI who to be.
Prompt: "Act as an expert travel agent specializing in budget travel. Create a 5-day itinerary for a trip to Rome for a solo traveler who loves history and food."
slides.narration:
Here's a bonus tip: provide a Persona.
Tell the AI who it should act as.
For example, 'Act as an expert travel agent.'
This is a super-powerful trick.
It helps the AI adopt a specific role.
slides.image_prompt: AI robot wearing a suit and glasses, acting as an expert.

slides.title: Giving Examples: Zero-Shot
content: Zero-Shot: You give zero examples.
You just ask for what you want.
Most prompts are zero-shot.
slides.narration:
We can also give examples to the AI.
This is called Zero-Shot prompting.
You give zero examples to the AI.
You just ask for what you want directly.
Our previous examples were all zero-shot.
slides.image_prompt: AI robot with a question mark, no examples given.

slides.title: Giving Examples: One-Shot
content: One-Shot: You give one example.
Great for specific formatting.

Prompt: "Summarize text into key points like this: Text: 'The sun is a star, and it's the center of our solar system.' Output: 'Primary celestial body: Sun'
Now, use this format for the following text: [insert long article here]"
slides.narration:
Next is One-Shot prompting.
Here, you give one example.
This shows the AI the format you want.
It's great for specific formatting.
The AI then follows this pattern.
slides.image_prompt: AI robot with one example, then an arrow to a new task.

slides.title: Giving Examples: Few-Shot
content: Few-Shot: You give a few examples.
Teaches AI a more complex pattern.
slides.narration:
Finally, there is Few-Shot prompting.
You give a few examples to the AI.
This teaches the AI a more complex pattern.
It helps the AI understand nuanced tasks.
slides.image_prompt: AI robot with multiple examples, then an arrow to a new task.

slides.title: Summary
content: Weak prompts get weak answers.
Great prompts use Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
Clarity makes prompts specific.
Context provides background.
Constraints set rules for the output.
Bonus tips include Persona and Examples.
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, we learned about prompt quality.
Weak prompts give weak answers.
Great prompts use Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
Clarity helps us be specific.
Context provides necessary background.
Constraints set rules for the output.
We also explored Persona and Examples.
slides.image_prompt: Infographic summarizing the 3 Cs and bonus tips.

slides.title: Assignment
content: Practice writing prompts for an AI.
Use Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
Task: Write a prompt for an AI to generate a recipe.
Make it a "one-shot" prompt.
It should be for a vegan, gluten-free dessert.
The output should include ingredients and step-by-step instructions.
The recipe name should be at the top.
slides.narration:
Here is a small assignment for you.
Practice writing prompts for an AI.
Use Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
Your task is to write a prompt for an AI to generate a recipe.
Make it a "one-shot" prompt.
It should be for a vegan, gluten-free dessert.
The output should include ingredients and step-by-step instructions.
And the recipe name should be at the top.
slides.image_prompt: Person working on a laptop with a thought bubble of a recipe.
